body.input: Which software companies opened an office in Norway in 2026?

response.content:
Based on available information, the following software company has been confirmed as opening an office in Norway in 2026:

- **Arondite** — A British military software developer (specializing in AI-enabled mission orchestration software) announced in November 2026 that it is opening its first international office in **Oslo, Norway**. The company plans to invest £35 million (approximately NOK 430 million) over five years to scale its work with the Norwegian Armed Forces, Norwegian industry, and NATO allies. The expansion was announced alongside a contract with UK Commando Force, and the Oslo office will support collaboration on European security in the High North.

No comprehensive list of all software companies that opened offices in Norway during 2026 was found. Other tech-related expansions mentioned in the context of Norway in 2026 relate primarily to data center developments (e.g., Microsoft, Nscale, CoreWeave), though these are infrastructure/data center operations rather than traditional office openings.

explainability.content: The source dated 12 November 2026 reports that Arondite announced it is expanding to Norway by opening its first international office in Oslo, confirming the company’s office opening in Norway in 2026.

A separate article describing Arondite as a British military software developer states it will invest NOK 430 million as it opens its first office outside the UK in Oslo, reinforcing that the office opening is a software‑company expansion in Norway in 2026.

context.content:
The Cobalt mission orchestration software will enable seamless co-ordination between UKCF, UK defence units and partner forces across the JEF coalition. It will also allow future hardware and AI capabilities to be deployed rapidly. UKCF and Arondite will make the platform available to Norwegian units for joint testing during upcoming deployments, in line with the JEF’s new Northern Navies Initiative announced by the First Sea Lord on the first day of Atlantic Future Forum.

Alongside the UKCF contract, Arondite today announced it is expanding to Norway, opening its first international office in Oslo. The company will invest £35 million over the next five years to scale its work with Norwegian Armed Forces, Norwegian industry and NATO allies. [...] From:
:   Ministry of Defence and Luke Pollard MP

Published:
:   12 November 2026

 

 British commandos will see operational effectiveness and warfighting readiness boosted with deployment of UK start-up Arondite’s advanced AI software.
 Multi-million pound deal comes as Arondite bring their cutting-edge British tech to Norway, strengthening collective Euro-Atlantic security.
 Announcement made at Atlantic Future Forum, the UK’s flagship international security conference and a unique demonstration of British convening power and strong partnerships across NATO. [...] ### Will Blyth, Co-founder and CEO of Arondite, said:

> UK Commando Force remain ready to defend the High North at a moment’s notice. As the threats we face become more complex and unpredictable, commando units are employing the latest technologies to reach further and adapt faster than our adversaries. It is a real privilege to support teams who are adopting technology at the speed modern deterrence demands.
>
> Our allies in Norway are working side-by-side with UK Commandos every day on the frontline of European security. They have some of the most complex missions in the world and they rightly demand technology that works from day one, which is why I am proud to announce Arondite’s first office outside of the UK will be in Oslo, as part of our long-term commitment to Norway.

document.name: UK Commandos to get AI-enabled edge from British scale-up Arondite, as company expands to NATO's northern flank - GOV.UK
